s87dc0252f5ea8d: First, the original K8s' “pity points”: why is it difficult to share GPU?
sb9aeabcd2db8b4: Before going deep into KAI, let us recall why GPU sharing in Kubernetes is a challenge in itself:
sd41b385ceb74f3: Integer limit: The Kubernetes Primary Resource Model (nvidia.com/gpu) only recognizes integer GPUs and does not express a need like "I want 0.2 GPUs".
secf00850282a89: Scheduling ignorance: the standard kube-scheduler cannot understand the concept of fraction GPU, which could have caused conflict by allocating a shared GPU to a Pod requesting a whole card.
s99ce0c98ef171f: Status "Black Box": How do Kubernetes know that a GPU has been partially occupied? Lack of standard representation.
s52f0fa1dd034b2: User inconvenient: Developer needs a simple visual way to apply for and use the score GPU resource.

s7475f226129453: In the face of these challenges, KAI-Scheduler offers a very clever solution:
s4bb7cf54f2c384: The core idea can be understood as a “logical deception”:
s86a49b3b6907c9: When a Pod requested points for GPU, KAI-Scheduler would not attempt directly to tell K8s "this Pod wants 0.0 x GPU".
sd7fe558bcd9f1b: Instead, it will create a special low-resource consumption Pod. This Pod will formally apply to Kubernetes for the entire GPU (nvidia.com/gpu: "1)!
sc7ba02f79e5fbc: So Kubernetes thinks this GPU has been completely distributed, and that kube-scheduler naturally will not put the other Pod Scheduling on this GPU again.
sc64caf7eeea824: The actual fractional management and distribution logic is maintained in-house by KAI-Scheduler.

sc552903010cd8a: IV. KAI Analysis of Probabilities and Shortfalls: Elegance and Possibilities
sbfc89bd12c8b3e: Let's analyse the characteristics of KAI-Scheduler GPU Share:
se194206fb83903: : Full use of the K8s standard original language (Pod, Annotication, Label), zero changes to the K8s core component and relatively simple deployment and integration.
s317428e5da45cd: : Reservation Pod was designed so as to avoid direct conflict with other components such as kube-scheduler.
sb9e18dc6da8b6f: : Theoretically supports the distribution of points for arbitrary ratios, without pre-sets.
s028ea511b4d857: The design idea of "logical deception" shows the ingenuity to expand capabilities within the existing framework of K8s.
s4db54afd7b25af: This is the central feature of its design. KAI-Scheduler does not provide any mandatory resource allocation (whether GPU memory or computing). It is only responsible for "logical" distribution and scheduling.
s8566864514acc8: : The actual use of resources relies entirely on the self-consciousness of the application running in Pod. One Pod can try to use 80% or even 100% GPU memory or compute resourcees, even if it only applies for gpu-training: "0.2. ". KAI Puscheduling does not prevent this.
s6dad8478699758: : This means that it cannot prevent the excessive use of resources by misapplications (whether unintentional or malicious), thereby interfering with other “neighbor” Pod on the same physical GPU, leading to performance shaking and even OOM.
sa175f7360fe09e: : In order to simulate the effects of solitude as much as possible, users must manually set resource limits within application codes (e.g. using a toolch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_action or a similar configuration for TensorFlow), which increases the complexity of use and potential error points.
sd6523553a8b615: V. Technical path comparison: lightweight vs HAMi hardsolization
sc1f745f09f3802: Now, let's compare KAI's program with the technical path of Hami:
s42c42bdb7ac976: The core strength of HAMi (and other GPU virtualization programs that seek to strengthen) lies in the realization of hard association. This is usually achieved by:
s09490dbdd82ba1: : Not just report resources, but inject the distribution configuration.
s4bb4dc9ff2e2d9: : Use of a lower-level interdiction between CUDA-Runtime and CUDA-Driver to use GPU GPU memory resources for each container
s27dbf16252bd56: The key advantages of hard-solation are:
sd3a4b0e64bacbe: : The GPU resources available for each container have a clear ceiling and cannot be over-occupied.
s89b42b58e8e60e: : Effectively prevent problems of “challenging neighbours” and guarantee the quality of services in a multi-tenant environment (QoS).
sdfcdf984fee9cb: : In most cases, user applications do not need to modify codes or add additional configurations.
s0fed676deaab13: Its deployment is simple, and it is very elegantly integrated with K8s. It provides a lightweight GPU sharing scheme.

s3e291bdd498557: VII. Summary: positive dialogue, cooperation for win-wins and a shared future
sf5b1d8b331e965: KAI-Scheduler GPU Shaping: Design elegance, compatibility with K8s ecology, smartly achieves the scores of the Scheduling level through Reservation Pod. But it's softism that relies on applied self-regulation.
sc4f2515a3069a1: HAMi: The pursuit of hard-tooling by providing mandatory resource limitations and guarantees through HAMi Device Plugin and HAMi-Core is more suited to a production environment with high demand for solitude.
s804b5fbea1e8de: Community and Cooperation: We appreciate the KAI team’s technological innovations, and welcome their opening up. Through active dialogue with the Run:ai (Nvidia) team in KubeCon EU, we see great potential for community collaboration.
s16c95ea9e410d5: The HAMi community will continue to focus on the development of KAI-Scheduler and actively participate in community discussions, looking forward to a stronger, more flexible and reliable GPU solution for Kubernetes users with partners including Nvidia/Run:ai.

s99832d0dfec7a1: HAMi, fully known as Heterogeneous AI Commanding Vitalization Middleware (heterogenouscomputation intermediate), is a “one-stop” structure designed to manage the heterogeneous AI computing equipment in k8s clusters that provides for the sharing of heterogenous AI equipment and provides inter-mission resource support. HAMi works to increase the utilization of the Heterogeneous computing equipment in K8s to provide a uniform interface for different types of heterogeneous devices. HAMi is currently a CNCF Sandbox project that has been incorporated into the CACI technical landscape.
